title: Sausage Gnocchi Skillet
shortDescription: Creamy tomato gnocchi with sausage and spinach
subtitle: Creamy tomato gnocchi with sausage and spinach
description: Italian sausage, pillowy gnocchi, tomato sauce, spinach, and mozzarella cook into a quick crew dinner.

steps.title: Heat skillet
steps.instruction: Heat a deep skillet over medium-high so sausage browns before the sauce is added.

steps.title: Brown sausage
steps.instruction: Cook sausage, breaking it into bite-size pieces until browned and no pink remains.

steps.title: Check sausage
steps.instruction: Confirm sausage reaches 165°F with a thermometer before continuing.

steps.title: Soften onion
steps.instruction: Add onion and cook until translucent, scraping any browned sausage bits into the pan.

steps.title: Add sauce
steps.instruction: Pour in marinara and a little water, then bring it to a gentle simmer.

steps.title: Cook gnocchi
steps.instruction: Stir gnocchi into sauce and simmer until tender; stir often so it does not stick.

steps.title: Wilt spinach
steps.instruction: Add spinach in handfuls and fold until it wilts into the hot sauce.

steps.title: Melt cheese
steps.instruction: Scatter mozzarella over the top, cover, and let residual steam melt it without scorching.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep the skillet covered above 140°F; loosen with hot water if gnocchi thickens.

steps.title: Spoon servings
steps.instruction: Serve immediately with a wide spoon so each portion includes sausage, gnocchi, and sauce.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Italian sausage — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Italian sausage and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use two skillets for faster service.
Do not boil gnocchi aggressively or it can break.
tonightSpread: Condiments: parmesan, red pepper flakes, basil
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Italian sausage in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: It is fast enough for a weeknight and needs only one skillet plus a side salad.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: slice sausage and grate cheese 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate 3 days. Reheating: heat sausage and sauce to 165°F.
substitutions: Use turkey sausage for pork sausage.
